es.summary: Acumulación excesiva de agua y sodio en el espacio intersticial e intravascular que supera la capacidad de regulación del organismo.
key_points: Puede ser consecuencia de insuficiencia cardíaca, renal o hepática.
Se manifiesta con edema periférico, aumento de peso y disnea.
Los laboratorios típicos incluyen Na+ > 145 mEq/L y BNP elevado.
El tratamiento combina restricción hídrica, diuréticos y control de la causa subyacente.

pathophysiology: Disminución del gasto cardíaco o filtración glomerular reduce la eliminación de agua y sodio.
Activación del sistema renina‑angiotensina‑aldosterona retiene Na+ y agua.
Aumento de la presión capilar favorece el paso de líquido al espacio intersticial.
El exceso de líquido produce edema y congestión pulmonar.
risk_factors: Enfermedad renal crónica o síndrome nefrótico.
Uso de corticoides o terapia hormonal.
signs_symptoms: Aumento de peso > 2 kg en 48 h.
Disnea de reposo o al esfuerzo.
diagnostics: Peso diario y registro de ingesta/salida (I/O).
Electrolitos séricos: Na+ > 145 mEq/L, K+ variable.
Ecocardiograma para valorar fracción de eyección.
treatment: Restricción de sodio a < 2 g/día y de líquidos según prescripción.
Control de la causa subyacente (ej. terapia de insuficiencia cardíaca).
Monitoreo estricto de I/O y peso.
complications: Riesgo de trombosis venosa profunda por estasis.
nursing_care: Evaluar peso, edema, respiración y signos de congestión cada 4 h.
Registrar ingesta y salida de líquidos; alertar si I/O > + 500 mL.
Mantener al paciente en posición semisentado para facilitar la respiración.
Administrar diuréticos según orden y observar respuesta clínica.
Vigilar electrolitos y función renal cada 24 h.
patient_teaching: Explicar la importancia de la restricción de sodio y líquidos.
Enseñar a registrar peso diario y reportar aumentos > 0.5 kg.
Instruir sobre signos de alerta: aumento de edema, disnea, dolor torácico.
Promover la adherencia a la medicación y citas de control.
Fomentar una dieta baja en sal y rica en frutas y verduras.

outcomes: Na+ sérico dentro de 135‑145 mEq/L en 5 días

interventions.action: Monitorear peso diario y registrar cambios de ±0.1 kg.
interventions.rationale: Detecta rápidamente la acumulación o pérdida de líquido.

interventions.action: Controlar ingesta y salida de líquidos cada 4 h.
interventions.rationale: Permite identificar desequilibrios de balance hídrico.

interventions.action: Aplicar restricción de sodio a < 2 g/día y líquidos según prescripción.
interventions.rationale: Reduce la retención de agua y mejora la presión arterial.

interventions.action: Administrar diurético de asa (furosemida) según orden y observar respuesta urinaria.
interventions.rationale: Facilita la eliminación de exceso de sodio y agua.

interventions.action: Evaluar signos de sobrecarga pulmonar (crepitantes, SpO2) cada 4 h.
interventions.rationale: Previene deterioro respiratorio y edema pulmonar.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre registro de peso y signos de alerta.
interventions.rationale: Promueve autocuidado y detección temprana de recaídas.

outcomes: Electrolitos séricos dentro de rango normal en 72 h
Sin síntomas de arritmia ni debilidad muscular

interventions.action: Obtener panel de electrolitos (Na+, K+, Cl-) cada 24 h.
interventions.rationale: Detecta alteraciones tempranas provocadas por diuréticos.

interventions.action: Alertar al médico ante K+ < 3.5 mEq/L o Na+ > 145 mEq/L.
interventions.rationale: Previene complicaciones cardíacas y neuromusculares.

interventions.action: Administrar suplementos de potasio oral o IV según indicación.
interventions.rationale: Corrige hipokalemia y reduce riesgo de arritmias.

interventions.action: Reforzar educación sobre alimentos ricos en potasio y bajo en sodio.
interventions.rationale: Apoya el mantenimiento de electrolitos en rango terapéutico.

interventions.action: Monitorear ritmo cardíaco y presión arterial cada 4 h.
interventions.rationale: Identifica efectos de desequilibrios electrolíticos en la función cardíaca.

en.summary: Excessive accumulation of water and sodium in the interstitial and intravascular spaces that exceeds the body's regulatory capacity.
key_points: May result from heart, kidney, or liver failure.
Manifests with peripheral edema, weight gain, and dyspnea.
Typical labs include Na+ > 145 mEq/L and elevated BNP.
Treatment combines fluid restriction, diuretics, and control of the underlying cause.

pathophysiology: Reduced cardiac output or glomerular filtration decreases elimination of water and sodium.
Activation of the renin‑angiotensin‑aldosterone system retains Na+ and water.
Increased capillary pressure favors fluid shift into the interstitial space.
Excess fluid produces edema and pulmonary congestion.
risk_factors: Chronic kidney disease or nephrotic syndrome.
Use of corticosteroids or hormonal therapy.
diagnostics: Serum electrolytes: Na+ > 145 mEq/L, K+ variable.
treatment: Sodium restriction < 2 g/day and fluid restriction per prescription.
Control of underlying cause (e.g., heart failure therapy).
complications: Risk of deep vein thrombosis from stasis.
nursing_care: Assess weight, edema, breathing, and congestion signs every 4 h.
Record fluid intake and output; alert if I/O > + 500 mL.
Keep patient in semi‑upright position to aid breathing.
Administer diuretics as ordered and observe clinical response.
Monitor electrolytes and renal function every 24 h.
patient_teaching: Explain importance of sodium and fluid restriction.
Teach daily weight recording and reporting increases > 0.5 kg.
Instruct on warning signs: increased edema, dyspnea, chest pain.
Encourage medication adherence and follow‑up appointments.
Promote a low‑salt diet rich in fruits and vegetables.

outcomes: Serum Na+ within 135‑145 mEq/L in 5 days

interventions.action: Monitor daily weight and record changes of ±0.1 kg.
interventions.rationale: Rapidly detects fluid accumulation or loss.

interventions.action: Control intake and output every 4 h.
interventions.rationale: Identifies fluid balance imbalances.

interventions.action: Apply sodium restriction < 2 g/day and fluid restriction per prescription.
interventions.rationale: Reduces water retention and improves blood pressure.

interventions.action: Administer loop diuretic (furosemide) as ordered and observe urine output.
interventions.rationale: Facilitates elimination of excess sodium and water.

interventions.action: Assess signs of pulmonary overload (crackles, SpO2) every 4 h.
interventions.rationale: Prevents respiratory deterioration and pulmonary edema.

interventions.action: Educate patient on weight recording and warning signs.
interventions.rationale: Promotes self‑care and early detection of relapse.

outcomes: Serum electrolytes within normal range in 72 h
No arrhythmia or muscle weakness symptoms

interventions.action: Obtain electrolyte panel (Na+, K+, Cl-) every 24 h.
interventions.rationale: Detects early changes caused by diuretics.

interventions.action: Alert physician if K+ < 3.5 mEq/L or Na+ > 145 mEq/L.
interventions.rationale: Prevents cardiac and neuromuscular complications.

interventions.action: Administer oral or IV potassium supplements as indicated.
interventions.rationale: Corrects hypokalemia and reduces arrhythmia risk.

interventions.action: Reinforce education on potassium‑rich and low‑sodium foods.
interventions.rationale: Supports maintenance of electrolytes within therapeutic range.

interventions.action: Monitor heart rhythm and blood pressure every 4 h.
interventions.rationale: Identifies effects of electrolyte imbalances on cardiac function.

key_points.1.quote: Swelling and weight gain from fluid in your ankles, lower legs, or abdomen (belly).

sections.pathophysiology.3.quote: Symptoms of fluid overload include pitting edema, ascites, and dyspnea and crackles from fluid in the lungs.

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: Heart failure can affect one or both sides of your heart: With right-sided heart failure , your heart is too weak to pump enough blood to your lungs to get oxygen.

sections.risk_factors.2.quote: Patients at risk for developing FVE are those with the following conditions: cirrhosis heart failure kidney failure pregnancy Symptoms of fluid overload include pitting edema, ascites, and dyspnea and crackles from fluid in the lungs.

sections.diagnostics.1.quote: The normal serum sodium range is 135 to 145 mEq/L.

sections.treatment.1.quote: Potassium-wasting diuretics (loop diuretics and thiazide diuretics) are a common cause of hypokalemia.

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: Heart failure is a common chronic condition that often improves with diet and lifestyle modifications such as sodium restriction and fluid restriction.
